description: Kilo is the all-in-one agentic engineering platform. Build, ship, and iterate faster with the most popular open source coding agent.

The open source coding agent for building with AI in VS Code, JetBrains, or the CLI.

--- Kilo Code is an AI coding agent that meets you everywhere you work: [VS Code](https://kilo.ai/landing/vs-code), [JetBrains](https://kilo.ai/features/jetbrains-native), and the [CLI](https://kilo.ai/cli). It's open source with open pricing. You pick from 500+ models, switch between them mid-task, and pay the model provider's rate with zero markup. No API keys required to start. ### Installation Pick where you want to run Kilo.
VS Code
Install the [Kilo Code extension](vscode:extension/kilocode.kilo-code) directly, or grab it from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=kilocode.Kilo-Code). Create an account and you'll have access to 500+ models including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Grok 4.6, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, all at provider pricing.
CLI
```bash # npm npm install -g @kilocode/cli # curl curl -fsSL https://kilo.ai/cli/install | bash # pnpm pnpm add -g @kilocode/cli # bun bun add -g @kilocode/cli # Homebrew (macOS / Linux) brew install Kilo-Org/tap/kilo # Arch Linux (AUR) paru -S kilo-bin ``` Then run `kilo` in any project directory to start.
JetBrains
Install the [Kilo Code plugin](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/plugin/28350-kilo-code) from the JetBrains Marketplace, or search "Kilo Code" in `Settings → Plugins` inside any JetBrains IDE.
Cloud Agent
Run Kilo from the web, no local machine needed, at [app.kilo.ai/cloud](https://app.kilo.ai/cloud).
Code Reviews
Set up automated AI code reviews on your pull requests at [app.kilo.ai/code-reviews](https://app.kilo.ai/code-reviews).
Install the CLI from GitHub Releases (binaries) Download the latest binary from the [Releases page](https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/releases). | Platform | Asset | |---|---| | Windows (most PCs) | `kilo-windows-x64.zip` | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | `kilo-darwin-arm64.zip` | | macOS (Intel) | `kilo-darwin-x64.zip` | | Linux x64 | `kilo-linux-x64.tar.gz` | | Linux ARM | `kilo-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | Notes: `x64-baseline` is a compatibility build for older CPUs without AVX. `musl` is the statically linked build for Alpine or minimal Docker images without glibc. `kilo-vscode-*.vsix` is the VS Code extension package, not the CLI. `Source code` archives are for building from source.
### Agents Kilo ships with specialized agents you switch between depending on the task. You can also build your own custom agents. - **Code** - The default. Implements and edits code from natural language. - **Plan** - Designs architecture and writes implementation plans before any code gets written. - **Ask** - Answers questions about your codebase without touching any files. - **Debug** - Troubleshoots and traces issues. Learn more about [agents and custom agents](https://kilo.ai/docs/code-with-ai/agents/using-agents). ### What it does - **Code generation** from natural language, across multiple files. - **Inline autocomplete** with ghost-text suggestions and tab to accept. - **Self-checking** so the agent reviews and corrects its own work. - **Terminal and browser control** to run commands and automate the web. - **Kilo Marketplace** to install agents, skills, MCP servers, and plugins that extend what the agent can do. - **500+ models** with mid-task switching, so you can match latency, cost, and reasoning to the job. ### Autonomous Mode (CI/CD) Run `kilo run` with `--auto` for fully autonomous operation with no prompts, built for CI/CD pipelines: ```bash kilo run --auto "run tests and fix any failures" ``` `--auto` auto-approves permission prompts unless a rule explicitly denies the action. Only use it in trusted environments. ### Documentation For configuration and everything else, [head over to the docs](https://kilo.ai/docs). ### Contributing Contributions are welcome from developers, writers, and everyone in between. Start with the [Contributing Guide](/CONTRIBUTING.md) for environment setup, coding standards, and how to open a pull request. See [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) for the VS Code extension and CLI release process, and [packages/kilo-jetbrains/RELEASING.md](packages/kilo-jetbrains/RELEASING.md) for the JetBrains plugin. Please review our [Code of Conduct](/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before getting involved. ### License MIT. You're free to use, modify, and distribute this code, including commercially, as long as you keep the attribution and license notices. See [License](/LICENSE). ### FAQ
Where did Kilo CLI come from? Kilo CLI is a fork of [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode), enhanced to work within the Kilo agentic engineering platform.

releases.name: JetBrains 7.2.1-rc.7
releases.body:
### Added

- Agent Manager worktrees can now be moved into an existing section from the row context menu with a new **Move To** submenu.
- New Worktree, branch/PR import, and Create Cloud Workspace dialogs offer a section picker, defaulting to the selected section or the selected workspace's parent so new tasks land where you are working.
- Both creation dialogs support prompt dictation, so you can speak the initial prompt instead of typing it.

### Fixed

- Successful worktree creations no longer stay stuck spinning or showing a temporary lock when a background reload discovers the checkout first.
- Initial prompts now keep their selected mode, model, and reasoning level through failures, reopening the session, and IDE restarts, without overwriting newer composer drafts.
- Failed or uncertain prompts are recovered as editable drafts instead of being silently lost.
- New Agent Manager rows are inserted at the top of their section, keeping the newest work in view.
- **Move To** is hidden when no other section exists, and worktree startup resumes after an IDE reconnect.
- Voice input no longer takes over the global action shortcut, and Create cannot discard an active recording or pen

releases.name: JetBrains 7.2.1-rc.6
releases.body:
### Added

- Voice dictation input in the prompt, with a configurable shortcut, speech model discovery, and clear recording limits.
- Agent Manager sections: group worktrees into color-coded sections you can drag to reorder.

### Fixed

- Fixed freezes and crashes reported from IDE logs, including hosted workspace freezes and uninitialized editor background lookups.
- Markdown and overlay hover could crash the IDE; both now render safely.
- Agent Manager branch state now stays in sync: superseded branch polls are ignored, PR badges refresh after accepted branch reloads, and branch picker popups no longer update while closing.
- Worktree placement is retained across transient branch reloads, and removed Agent Manager layout entries are pruned.
- Section drag targets are more stable while reordering.
- Prompt highlight ownership is preserved when multiple controllers handle the same prompt.
- Telemetry no longer fails during plugin unload, and unavailable Windows native cleanup no longer logs failures.
- Fixed a platform API usage that failed plugin verification, so releases publish again.

### Changed

- Kilo charges are now settled from `usage.cost`, with upstream cost used only fo

releases.name: JetBrains 7.2.1-rc.3
releases.body:
### Added

- Cloud workspace management: create, switch, and delete Cloud (hosted) workspaces, remember the profile per repository, and apply organization profile defaults.
- Cloud sessions now share the worktree editor UI, with session titles and activity kept in sync and a running indicator for Cloud turns like local ones.
- Transcript find: search the session transcript with match highlighting and next/previous navigation that keeps working while a response is streaming.
- Worktrees are organized in a shared active tree, with an **Update from Base** action and row buttons that highlight on hover.
- Questions appear in the prompt navigator so pending agent questions are easier to find.
- Transcript messages are labeled for screen readers.

### Fixed

- The plugin now uses public platform APIs for tree hover painting, so Marketplace publishing passes plugin verification again.
- Cloud workspace delete confirmation is simplified, and **Set as default** is removed from the Cloud workspace dialog.
- Local MCP issues are hidden in Cloud sessions.
- Plugin tools whose arguments cannot be converted to JSON Schema no longer break tool loading.
- Questions stay open when background result

The open source coding agent for building with AI in VS Code, JetBrains, or the CLI.

Kilo Code is an AI coding agent that meets you everywhere you work: VS Code, JetBrains, and the CLI. It's open source with open pricing. You pick from 500+ models, switch between them mid-task, and pay the model provider's rate with zero markup. No API keys required to start.

Installation

Pick where you want to run Kilo.

VS Code

Install the Kilo Code extension directly, or grab it from the VS Code Marketplace. Create an account and you'll have access to 500+ models including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Grok 4.6, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, all at provider pricing.

CLI 
# npm
npm install -g @kilocode/cli

# curl
curl -fsSL https://kilo.ai/cli/install | bash

# pnpm
pnpm add -g @kilocode/cli

# bun
bun add -g @kilocode/cli

# Homebrew (macOS / Linux)
brew install Kilo-Org/tap/kilo

# Arch Linux (AUR)
paru -S kilo-bin

Then run kilo in any project directory to start.

JetBrains

Install the Kilo Code plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace, or search "Kilo Code" in Settings → Plugins inside any JetBrains IDE.

Cloud Agent

Run Kilo from the web, no local machine needed, at app.kilo.ai/cloud.

Code Reviews

Set up automated AI code reviews on your pull requests at app.kilo.ai/code-reviews.

Install the CLI from GitHub Releases (binaries)

Download the latest binary from the Releases page.

Platform Asset
Windows (most PCs) kilo-windows-x64.zip
macOS (Apple Silicon) kilo-darwin-arm64.zip
macOS (Intel) kilo-darwin-x64.zip
Linux x64 kilo-linux-x64.tar.gz
Linux ARM kilo-linux-arm64.tar.gz

Notes: x64-baseline is a compatibility build for older CPUs without AVX. musl is the statically linked build for Alpine or minimal Docker images without glibc. kilo-vscode-*.vsix is the VS Code extension package, not the CLI. Source code archives are for building from source.

Agents

Kilo ships with specialized agents you switch between depending on the task. You can also build your own custom agents.

  • Code - The default. Implements and edits code from natural language.
  • Plan - Designs architecture and writes implementation plans before any code gets written.
  • Ask - Answers questions about your codebase without touching any files.
  • Debug - Troubleshoots and traces issues.

Learn more about agents and custom agents.

What it does

  • Code generation from natural language, across multiple files.
  • Inline autocomplete with ghost-text suggestions and tab to accept.
  • Self-checking so the agent reviews and corrects its own work.
  • Terminal and browser control to run commands and automate the web.
  • Kilo Marketplace to install agents, skills, MCP servers, and plugins that extend what the agent can do.
  • 500+ models with mid-task switching, so you can match latency, cost, and reasoning to the job.

Autonomous Mode (CI/CD)

Run kilo run with --auto for fully autonomous operation with no prompts, built for CI/CD pipelines:

kilo run --auto "run tests and fix any failures"

--auto auto-approves permission prompts unless a rule explicitly denies the action. Only use it in trusted environments.

Documentation

For configuration and everything else, head over to the docs.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome from developers, writers, and everyone in between. Start with the Contributing Guide for environment setup, coding standards, and how to open a pull request. See RELEASING.md for the VS Code extension and CLI release process, and packages/kilo-jetbrains/RELEASING.md for the JetBrains plugin.

Please review our Code of Conduct before getting involved.

License

MIT. You're free to use, modify, and distribute this code, including commercially, as long as you keep the attribution and license notices. See License.

FAQ

Where did Kilo CLI come from?

Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode, enhanced to work within the Kilo agentic engineering platform.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, all-in-one agentic engineering platform integrating AI coding assistants into major IDEs and CLIs.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Kilo Code is a fully open-source agentic engineering platform designed to significantly accelerate complex software development workflows. It functions as a comprehensive coding agent that integrates directly and seamlessly into VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and the command-line interface. The platform supports a wide array of leading large language models, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. This extensive support allows developers to flexibly build and iterate on code using their preferred AI backend. By providing a unified interface across different local environments, it drastically streamlines the overall process of building applications with AI assistance.
keyFeatures: Cross-Platform IDE Integration: Integrates seamlessly into VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and terminal environments for a unified experience.
Multi-Model Support: Allows developers to utilize various AI models including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini interchangeably.
Agentic Engineering Assistant: Provides a comprehensive platform for building, shipping, and iterating on code faster with AI.
Open Source Core Architecture: Maintains an open-source codebase, allowing for community contributions, audits, and transparency.
Extensive Platform Localization: Supports over 20 languages natively, making the platform accessible to a global developer audience.

useCases.title: CLI-Based Automation
useCases.description: Engineers leverage the terminal interface to script and automate complex refactoring tasks using the coding agent natively.

useCases.title: AI Model Comparison
useCases.description: Teams switch between Claude and GPT within the same IDE environment to determine which model performs best for specific tasks.

useCases.title: Rapid Feature Prototyping
useCases.description: Founders utilize the agentic platform to quickly build and iterate on new features across multiple programming languages efficiently.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and development teams looking for a versatile, open-source AI coding assistant integrated directly into their tools. The platform simplifies complex workflows and accelerates development timelines.
